request: Show me how much I spent per month year to date.

plan.title: Spending per month year to date
plan.question: spending per month from the start of the year to today, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and total_eur

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en, whatever language the data is in
one figure over the ordered months and no second dimension
a line reads a run over time the most directly
the columns are the month and the euro figure, the figure last
year to date is the start of the year to today, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from the household's own dates
reasoning_code:
the shape is line, so the mark is lineY over the rows
the columns are month and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y
the euro axis names the domain over the amounts and needs no grid behind it

request: Where did my income go this quarter? Draw it as a flow.

plan.title: Where the money went this quarter
plan.question: spending of this quarter grouped into the household's own categories, as flows out of one source named 'Income', one row per category, the source and the target of a row must differ and no total row belongs in the result, columns source, target and amount_eur, every amount positive

       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur

       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur

GROUP BY month, merchant
ORDER BY month, merchant

since the summer is 2025-06-01 to today 2025-12-31, and every supermarket is matched by its booking text

request: Vergleiche aufsummiert, wie viel das Gemeinschaftskonto und das Privatkonto seit dem Sommer ausgegeben haben.

plan.title: Beide Konten aufsummiert seit dem Sommer
plan.question: die Ausgaben je Konto seit dem Sommeranfang, innerhalb jedes Kontos Monat fuer Monat aufaddiert, eine Zeile je Monat und Konto, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM', konto und cumulative_eur

sql:
WITH per_month AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, account AS konto, -SUM(amount) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY month, konto
)
SELECT month, konto, ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (PARTITION BY konto ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per_month
ORDER BY konto, month
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
aufsummiert ist ein laufender Gesamtstand, und verglichen werden die beiden Konten
eine Flaeche je Konto, also eine Flaeche mit Serie und Legende
die Spalten sind der Monat, das Konto und die aufaddierte Euro-Zahl, die Zahl zuletzt
seit dem Sommer ist 2025-06-01 bis heute, 2025-12-31, aus den Daten des Haushalts gelesen
reasoning_code:
the shape is area and these rows carry a series, so one areaY and one lineY over all of them
the columns are month, konto and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
konto names the series, so it is the z and the color channel on both marks, and the tooltip names the account
the two bands are compared and not added, so each rests on zero itself: y1 zero, y2 the figure

request: Zeig als Fluss, wie unser Einkommen dieses Quartal auf die Ausgabengruppen verteilt wurde.

sql:
SELECT 'Einkommen' AS source,
       CASE WHEN description LIKE '%MIETE%' THEN 'Wohnen'
            WHEN description LIKE '%REWE%' THEN 'Lebensmittel'
            ELSE 'Sonstiges' END AS target,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY target
ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

ein Sankey zeichnet genau diesen Fluss
die Spalten sind Quelle, Ziel und der positive Euro-Betrag, die Zahl zuletzt
dieses Quartal ist 2025-10-01 bis 2025-12-31, und die Zielgruppen werden aus dem Buchungstext gebildet
reasoning_code:
the shape is sankey, so sankeyDiagram lays the flow out
the columns are source, target and amount_eur, and amount_eur holds the numbers
the nodes are the names of both ends, collected from the rows themselves
the child marks read the layout's own fields (x0, x1, y0, y1, key), never a column of the query
